title: Add art for each release
thread: **Issue #2681 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #2681: Add art for each release Opened by @jgoetzmann. Create art with cards effected for each release. The art should be full screen and animated on large releases (e.g., v0.3, v0.4). Make art for all past patches & make a process so there is art going forward for every patch. See if you can plop it into the releases on github too ## Plan _Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41316970750)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal Give every shipped patch, past and future, a deterministic 1920×1080 release artwork assembled from the public art of cards that patch changed, with a card-back composition when the patch changed no catalog row. Show the artwork on Patch notes, animate canonically classified major releases such as v0.3.0 and v0.4.0 while honoring reduced motion, and embed the deployed asset in the already-generated GitHub release body so the existing release publisher backfills old releases and handles every new patch without hand-authored art. ## Files to touch | Path | Kind | Change | | --- | --- | --- | | `apps/web/src/cards/art/svg.ts` | change | Export `proceduralCardArtUri`, the pure CardDef-to-existing-card-art URI adapter used by release compositions. | | `apps/web/src/cards/art/CardArt.test.tsx` | change | Prove the adapter matches `CardArt` for ordinary, Stinkyscape, Training Grounds, and Legacy art. | | `apps/web/src/patches/constants.ts` | change | Add the named release-art canvas, card-limit, and major-animation constants. | | `apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.ts` | new | Select affected definitions, render deterministic escaped SVGs, name their URLs, and build/resolve normal and still assets. | | `apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.test.ts` | new | Cover selection, zero-card fallback, SVG/motion output, URL lookup, and the complete real patch history. | | `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx` | change | Add `ReleaseArtwork` to every `PatchEntry`, using the still major asset in-app so CSS owns app motion. | | `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx` | change | Assert every rendered patch has the right artwork and major/static behavior. | | `apps/web/src/patches/patches.css` | change | Size the 16:9 artwork, animate only major artwork, and stop it for OS/app reduced motion. | | `apps/web/src/patches/testids.ts` | change | Add `patchTestid.releaseArt`. | | `apps/web/static-pages.ts` | change | Write all release SVGs into the Vite output and serve the same generated assets in development. | | `apps/web/src/static-pages.test.ts` | change | Prove the build writer emits the expected fixture art files. | | `apps/web/src/patches/github.ts` | change | Put the appropriate production/staging release-art image URL in every generated GitHub release body. | | `apps/web/src/patches/github.test.ts` | change | Assert historical/current release bodies embed the correct host and asset. | | `docs/issues-and-patches.md` | change | Document that art is generated from patch snapshots, what majors/zero-card patches do, and that GitHub publication is automatic. | Do not touch `crates/`, `spec/`, `e2e/`, any manifest or lockfile, or `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, or `.claude/`. This is presentation over public patch/catalog data under SPEC §5 and §10.10, CLAUDE.md rule 7, and R388, R507, R724000, R724001, and R1369000; it needs no rules decision, spec edit, patch fragment, or new ruling. ## Steps 1. In `apps/web/src/cards/art/svg.ts`, add `proceduralCardArtUri(def, radiant)` for the CardDef fields `id`, `name`, `tags`, and `type`. Mirror `CardArt.tsx` exactly: Training Grounds Legacy definitions use `snapshotArtOf` and the Core name without `LEGACY_PREFIX`; Stinkyscape and non-Legacy Training Grounds use their set-specific URI builders; all other definitions use `themeFor`, `compositionFor`, and `motifFor`. Import this pure, CSS-free module directly from `releaseArt.ts` (as `static-pages.ts` must load it in Node); do not change card rendering or the browser-only art barrel. 2. In `apps/web/src/patches/constants.ts`, name the generator values `RELEASE_ART_WIDTH` (1920), `RELEASE_ART_HEIGHT` (1080), `RELEASE_ART_CARD_LIMIT` (7), and `RELEASE_ART_MAJOR_CYCLE_SECONDS` (18). In new `apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.ts`, define `ReleaseArtMotion = "animated" | "still"`, `ReleaseArtAsset`, and `ReleaseArtInput`, plus XML escaping and internal layout helpers whose geometry is expressed through named constants. 3. Implement `releaseArtCards(patch, after, before)` in `releaseArt.ts`. Walk `patch.changes` in recorded order; resolve added/changed IDs from `after` and removed IDs from `before`; throw a version-and-ID error if a claimed definition is missing; deduplicate IDs. Keep all candidates up to `RELEASE_ART_CARD_LIMIT`; above it, choose exactly that many evenly across the ordered list, including the first and last, so a large set release is representative without hand curation. Do not infer card IDs from prose: an empty `changes` list deliberately yields the generic card-back composition. 4. Implement `releaseArtSvg({ patch, release, major, before, after }, motion)`. Return a self-contained, deterministic 1920×1080 SVG with an escaped release-line name, version, player title, and card names; a layered `` montage built from `proceduralCardArtUri` for `releaseArtCards`; and a decorative card-back montage when there are no candidates. Only `major === true` with `motion === "animated"` gets the slow pan/parallax keyframes using `RELEASE_ART_MAJOR_CYCLE_SECONDS`, with an embedded `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule that holds the complete composition still; the `still` form and every patch/micro form contain no animation. Use no random source, remote resource, script, hidden state, or engine data. 5. Add `releaseArtPath(version, motion)`, `releaseArtAssets(patches, snapshot, releases = RELEASES)`, and `releaseArtAsset(path, patches, snapshot, releases = RELEASES)` to `releaseArt.ts`. Paths are `/release-art/.svg` and `…/-still.svg`; emit the normal file for every patch and the still companion only where `majors(patches)` says major (recorded tier first, R1369000's historical fallback otherwise). Place versions into release lines with `releaseGroups`, preserve `patches.json` order, and carry the previous snapshot forward so removals use their last definition. 6. Extend `apps/web/static-pages.ts` without adding another Vite plugin. Let `StaticPagesInput` optionally carry patch snapshots; when present, `writeStaticPages` writes every `releaseArtAssets` entry beneath `outDir/release-art/`. In `staticPages()`, remove the build-only restriction, keep the existing build behavior, load every shipped snapshot for `writeBundle`, and add a `configureServer` middleware that recognizes only `releaseArtAsset` paths, generates from the JSON files under `crates/cards/patches/`, returns `image/svg+xml`, and delegates every unknown path. Do not write generated files into the source tree. 7. In `PatchNotes.tsx`, compute a `Set` of canonical major versions once from `majors(patches)`, pass `major` through `ReleaseBubble` and `PatchEntry`, and add a local `ReleaseArtwork({ patch, major })` immediately after each `patch__head`. Render a decorative lazy `` with empty alt, `patchTestid.releaseArt`, the version/major state in data attributes, and `releaseArtPath`; majors use the `still` asset because page CSS supplies motion, while all others use the normal static asset. In `patches.css`, give the artwork a clipped 16:9 full-screen canvas presentation at the available width and a stable fallback background; drift/scale only a major image under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and `:root:not([data-reduce-motion="true"])`, leaving a complete still composition otherwise. Use the existing palette, type, surface, and motion conventions and avoid affecting patch collapsing or lazy snapshot reads. 8. In `github.ts`, add the Markdown image immediately after the date/release/tier line in `body`: descriptive escaped alt text and the normal `releaseArtPath` under the same `site` already chosen for the footer (staging for a prerelease, production for a live release). Keep it outside the card-detail fallback so every detail level retains the art. No workflow edit is needed: `.github/workflows/releases.yml` already reruns for `github.ts`, rewrites all releases, and future `patches.json` ships already trigger it. 9. Update `docs/issues-and-patches.md`'s GitHub releases/process section: every shipped patch automatically gets the generated asset; affected definitions come only from the snapshot diff, removals use the preceding snapshot, zero-card patches use backs, R1369000's canonical major classification—not change count—selects the animated form, and the release generator embeds the build host's URL. State that maintainers never add per-version image files or hand-edit GitHub release art. 10. Add the tests below, run them, then inspect `git diff --check` and `git status --short` to confirm that no generated `dist/` output or forbidden/unrelated file is included. ## Tests - `apps/web/src/cards/art/CardArt.test.tsx`, add `it("#2681 proceduralCardArtUri matches CardArt's generated source for every art family")`: compare the helper URI with rendered Core, Stinkyscape, Training Grounds, and Legacy windows on base and Radiant faces. - `apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.test.ts`, add tests named `it("#2681 selects only definitions affected by the patch in recorded order")`, `it("#2681 samples a large patch deterministically and draws backs for a zero-card patch")`, `it("#2681 emits byte-identical escaped full-screen SVG and animates only the normal form of a major")`, `it("#2681 resolves only canonical normal and major-still asset paths")`, and `it("#2681 gives every real shipped patch an artwork and every real major a still companion")`. - `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`, add `it("#2681 shows generated artwork for every patch and uses CSS-owned still art for majors")`; assert source paths, lazy/decorative image semantics, tiers, and the reduced-motion CSS gates without snapshot fetches beyond the existing contract. - `apps/web/src/static-pages.test.ts`, add `it("#2681 writes normal release art for every patch and a still companion for each major")` using fixture snapshots and a temporary output directory. - `apps/web/src/patches/github.test.ts`, add `it("#2681 embeds each release's artwork from staging or production as appropriate")`, and extend the real-history assertion so every body names its encoded tag's SVG. Run exactly: ```sh pnpm --dir apps/web test src/cards/art/CardArt.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/releaseArt.test.ts pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web test src/static-pages.test.ts pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/github.test.ts pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/cards/art/svg.ts apps/web/src/cards/art/CardArt.test.tsx apps/web/src/patches/constants.ts apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.ts apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.test.ts apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx apps/web/src/patches/testids.ts apps/web/static-pages.ts apps/web/src/static-pages.test.ts apps/web/src/patches/github.ts apps/web/src/patches/github.test.ts pnpm --dir apps/web build cargo fmt --check cargo jackioh catalog check cargo jackioh patches check cargo jackioh spec check git diff --check ``` ## Done when - [ ] Every entry in the real `patches.json`, including zero-card patches, has a deterministic 1920×1080 artwork generated from tracked public data, with no per-version source asset. - [ ] Canonical major art has an animated normal SVG and still companion; Patch notes animates it only when both OS and app motion settings permit. - [ ] Patch/micro art is static, and cards shown in any montage are definitions that patch actually added, changed, or removed. - [ ] Patch notes displays the artwork without changing release/patch collapse behavior or eager-loading historical snapshots. - [ ] Generated GitHub bodies embed the staging asset for prereleases and production asset for live releases, so the existing publisher backfills history and future ships need no manual step. - [ ] The five targeted Vitest files, web typecheck, targeted ESLint, and production web build pass. - [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, catalog check, patches check, spec check, and `git diff --check` pass; no `dist/`, generated source, forbidden path, manifest, lockfile, spec, catalog, or patch data is changed. ## Risks - Snapshot correctness: removed art must come from the preceding snapshot and added/changed art from the resulting snapshot; fail generation on missing claimed IDs instead of silently showing an unrelated card. - Determinism/replay: use patch order and pure ID-derived card art only—no clock, OS randomness, hash iteration, engine state, replay state, or mutable selection—so the same history produces byte-identical SVGs. - Hidden information: patch snapshots are public catalog data under R388; neither the component nor generator reads a match, `EngineState`, or anything beyond public definitions, preserving CLAUDE.md rule 7. - Motion/accessibility: external animated SVG state cannot see the app setting, so the app deliberately loads the still major file and owns its animation in CSS; both the media query and root setting stop it. GitHub receives the animated SVG, whose own embedded `prefers-reduced-motion` rule must also freeze it. - GitHub/deployment ordering: release Markdown points to the host selected by the existing prerelease/live logic. The URL may resolve only after that host's build finishes, but no GitHub credential or workflow change is needed and the next existing publisher run reconciles the body. - Contract drift: centralize URL and SVG generation in `releaseArt.ts`, reuse the existing CardArt families through `proceduralCardArtUri`, and prove the real history so a future patch automatically fails tests/build if its snapshot cannot produce art. ## Open questions None. Treat R1369000's canonical major classification (recorded tier, with its historical fallback) as “large release”; using a raw affected-card threshold was rejected because release size is already explicit data and historical high-card-count cleanup patches are not major releases. Treat “full screen” as a 1920×1080 16:9 asset that scales to the Patch notes width and GitHub surface, not a browser Fullscreen API interaction. ````
